title: CoFEH: LLM-driven Feature Engineering Empowered by Collaborative Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization

problem.claim: Traditional feature engineering methods are bottlenecked by rigid search spaces and limited domain awareness, while greedy FE-then-HPO workflows fail to capture strong feature-engineering and hyperparameter-optimization interactions.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based methods focus on isolated feature-engineering subtasks and are rarely coupled with downstream hyperparameter optimization for free-form, jointly optimized pipelines.

contributions.claim: CoFEH is a collaborative framework that interleaves LLM-based feature engineering and Bayesian hyperparameter optimization for end-to-end AutoML.

The framework combines Tree-of-Thought LLM-driven feature-engineering optimization, Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter optimization, and a dynamic optimizer selector that interleaves both steps.
A mutual conditioning mechanism shares context between the LLM and Bayesian optimizer to inform their decisions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CoFEH outperforms traditional and LLM-based baselines in standalone feature engineering and joint feature-engineering plus hyperparameter-optimization settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Feature engineering is important in AutoML but remains a bottleneck for traditional methods.
LLM-based approaches provide semantic reasoning but do not adequately support free-form pipelines or joint feature-engineering and hyperparameter optimization.
CoFEH interleaves LLM-based feature engineering and Bayesian hyperparameter optimization through flexible pipeline search, dynamic selection, and mutual conditioning.
The authors report superior performance against traditional and LLM-based baselines across standalone and joint settings.

source_observation.claim: The framework shares context between feature-engineering and hyperparameter-optimization components and adaptively interleaves their steps.

interpretation.claim: When two optimization stages interact strongly, coordinating their decisions may be more effective than optimizing them sequentially.

application.claim: Use shared state and adaptive alternation when designing pipelines with coupled search decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when joint coordination is preferable to sequential optimization or how much benefit comes from each component.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, metrics, baseline configurations, or quantitative performance differences.
The abstract does not describe the optimization objective, computational cost, or reproducibility details.
